items.title: SERVER: the one-shot owners the server `ui` twin makes for `when`, `when_live`, `swap`, `each` rows and `when_some` are never disposed, so whatever a body registers with its owner - a subscription, an `on_cleanup`, B693's keeper - stays on the store for the process's life, one per render
items.kind: bug (std process/web/ui; owner lifetime; leak per server render)
items.discussion: lane b693 (post-Order 55); `Conditional::place` (process/web/ui.vl ~:639), `place_swap` (~:680), `place_each` (~:704, ~:739) and `place_when_some` (~:956) each do `let owner = Owner::new(); run_with_owner(owner, \|\| ..)` and never `owner.dispose()`. A server render hears no later change, so the subscriptions are dead weight; with B693 each server render of a `when_live`/`when_remote_live` body over a long-lived store leaves one keeper feed on that store's flag node, and every keeper copies the payload once when the variant ends. Kolt's server renders no views today (no `render(` of the process twin), so it is not exposed; a server that SSRs pages over a long-lived store is
items.body: The browser twin disposes a body's owner when the boundary goes; the server twin, which renders once, has no boundary end and so never disposes. Rec: dispose each one-shot owner right after its body has placed its view - the render is the body's whole life on the server (`let row = run_with_owner(owner, ..); owner.dispose();`), which runs `on_cleanup`s at the right moment too; pin with `store_feed_census` (a server `render` of `when_live` over a store leaves 0 feeds) and the existing server-twin pins unchanged. Alternatively a request-scoped root owner the five sites parent under, disposed at the end of `render`. Sizing S.

items.title: A read below any store handle copies the handle's PATH lists on the way down - about 74 `__clone` calls per read of a five-step path, whatever the payload's size (`child_path`, the handle's `path`/`gate` fields)
items.kind: perf (std reactive store core; path lists)
items.discussion: lane b693 (post-Order 55); measured with the inference harness's `__clone` counter (`copies_per_print`, store.rs `B693_PHASES`): 100 reads of `live.records().at(1).some().title().get()` at 1,000 records cost 7,400 `__clone` calls after B693 (807,800 before) - 74 per read at any size, all of them copies of `List<StoreStep>` path lists as each projection builds `child_path(self.path, step)` and the handle structs copy `path` and `gate`
items.body: Every projection allocates and copies the path list of its parent plus one step, and each handle struct literal copies the list again (`root = self.root, path = self.path, gate = self.gate`); a five-step read builds five handles. The payload copy B689/B693 removed was the big term; this is the remaining per-read constant (~10 us on node). Rec: share the path - a persistent cons-list of steps (`Shared<PathNode>` parent pointers: a child's path is one allocation pointing at its parent's, equality/hashing by walking), or build the path lazily only when a slot is asked for (`watch_at`/`identity_at` need it; a plain `get` does not). Measure on kolt's leaf keystroke before choosing. Sizing M.

items.title: `check_hygiene.py` has exited 1 on proposals main since before 5b970199: five proposal files have no row in proposal/README.md (terminal.md, tuple-module.md, type-ascription.md, unit-literal.md, visibility.md)
items.discussion: integrator 2026-11-02; `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py` on main prints `proposal/README.md: <file> has 0 index rows (want exactly 1)` for the five and exits 1 beside the long-standing absolute-home-path offenders under scripts/integration (runner/, order37-39 sweeps, lsp-tip-9fab0ff5.json)
items.body: The README's one-row-per-file rule is enforced by the script but the five papers landed without rows (Order 48 for type-ascription/unit-literal/visibility; terminal.md and tuple-module.md later), so the gate has been red for a reason nobody acted on - which is how B689's missing `hash-map-lend.md` row was nearly missed too. Rec: add the five rows (status read from each file's own header), and decide the absolute-path offenders: the runner's Dockerfile/compose/entrypoint paths are CONTAINER paths (`/home/runner`) and should be allowed by the check (a `/home/runner` exemption or a per-line marker), the order37-39 sweep scripts and lsp-tip-9fab0ff5.json are records of the machine they ran on (allowlist the sweeps directories as records, or strip). Then `check_hygiene.py` exits 0 and can be a commit gate in the records sweep. Sizing S.
